body.statement:
Fix an admissible query \(z_0\).  Every labelled point
\(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\in
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) satisfies
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}\!\left[
 \{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_s\}W
 \right]=0
\]
for every cohort \(s\), unit \(i\), and bounded
\(\mathcal X\)-measurable random variable \(W\).  Hence each
\(E\in\mathcal X\) with \(0<\mathbb K_\xi(E)<1\) has treated mean
\(\mu_s\) on both \(E\) and \(E^c\), and
\texttt{lem:common-design-shock-obstruction} excludes the former
common-design-shock kernel.  For each
\(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), these conclusions transfer to its
associated labelled regular conditional point \(\xi_P(z_0)\) for
\(P\)-almost every query \(z_0\), with no assertion at query-null versions.
Nevertheless, there are admissible scalar fixed class parameters and, for
every positive \(N,T,n_1\), two labelled points
\(\xi^{(0)},\xi^{(1)}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}(z_0)\), with causal-data
kernels \(\mathbb K_0,\mathbb K_1\) and corresponding degenerate-query laws
\(P^{(0)},P^{(1)}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}\), having the same joint law of
\((X_{1t},Q_{1ti},Z_j)\) and the same target \(\tau(z_0)=0\), while
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb K_0}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X)=0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb K_1}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X)
 =\frac1{16}.
\]
Thus removal of the invalid witness is a necessary model repair, not a
determination of the sharp constants for the remaining centered fixed-query
product experiment.
body.justification: The theorem records what centering excludes in the fixed-query class, supplies an explicit two-kernel variance certificate, and applies the audit to \(\xi_P(z_0)\) almost everywhere.
body.gap: Exact constants for the remaining centered fixed-query optimal-recovery product experiment remain open.
body.consumer: The model audit removes the obsolete negative answer without treating a bare kernel as a labelled point or selecting a null conditional version.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(z_0\) and
\(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\in
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Boundedness makes all following
expectations finite, and design centering gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 [B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_s\mid\mathcal X]=0.              \tag{1}
\]
For bounded \(\mathcal X\)-measurable \(W\), the pull-out and tower
properties imply
\[
 \mathbb E[(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_s)W]
 =\mathbb E\!\left[W\,
   \mathbb E(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_s\mid\mathcal X)\right]=0. \tag{2}
\]
Taking \(W=\mathbf1_E\) gives
\(\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mathbf1_E]=\mu_s\mathbb K_\xi(E)\).
Division by \(\mathbb K_\xi(E)>0\), and the analogous argument for \(E^c\)
when \(\mathbb K_\xi(E)<1\), prove that both conditional means equal
\(\mu_s\).  Lemma \texttt{lem:common-design-shock-obstruction} then gives
the stated exclusion.  By the corrected Lemma
\texttt{lem:panel-fixed-query-kernel-transfer}, the same argument applies to
the labelled point \(\xi_P(z_0)\), rather than to its bare kernel, for
marginal-almost-every query of every panel law.

It remains to construct the variance certificate.  For arbitrary positive
\(N,T,n_1\), take
\[
 S=1,\quad\pi_1=1,\quad H=0,\quad p=d=1,\quad z_0=\tfrac12,
 \quad\lambda=\kappa=1,\quad B=L=1,\quad\delta_0=\tfrac14,  \tag{3}
\]
and \(c_X=C_X=c_\Sigma=C_\Sigma=1\).  Let
\((X_{1t})_t\), \((\eta_j)_j\), and \((\varepsilon_i)_i\) be mutually
independent, with \(X_{1t}\) i.i.d. uniform on \([0,1]\) and \(\eta_j\),
\(\varepsilon_i\) i.i.d. Rademacher.  Define
\[
 m_1(x)=\tfrac12,\qquad Q_{1ti}=\tfrac12,
 \qquad Z_j=\tfrac12+\eta_j.                                 \tag{4}
\]
Set \(W_{1i,-1}=1/2\), \(R_{1i0}(0)=0\), and therefore
\(B_{1i}(0)=1/2\).  Under \(\mathbb K_0\), set \(R_{1i0}(1)=0\); under
\(\mathbb K_1\), set \(R_{1i0}(1)=\varepsilon_i/2\).  Consistency gives
\[
 B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=\tfrac12\quad(\mathbb K_0),
 \qquad
 B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=\tfrac12+\tfrac14\varepsilon_i
 \quad(\mathbb K_1).                                        \tag{5}
\]
The smallest return is \(-1/2>-1\), so the return support is respected.

Give both kernels labels \(\mu_1=1/2\), \(m_1\) from (4), and
\(\Sigma=1\).  Wealth is bounded by one, the constant regression lies in
\(\mathcal H_1(1,1)\), and \(z_0\) is interior.  The uniform design has
density one and beta-mixing coefficients zero.  Conditional on
\(\mathcal X\), histories are independent across \(i\), and
\[
 \mathbb E[Q_{1ti}\mid\mathcal X]=\tfrac12=m_1(X_{1t}),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E[B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X]
 =\mathbb E B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=\tfrac12=\mu_1.            \tag{6}
\]
Thus the treated mean is common across replicas; no identical-distribution
or within-history independence premise is used.  Donors are independent of
the panel and satisfy
\[
 \mathbb EZ_j=z_0,
 \qquad\operatorname{Var}(Z_j)=1,
 \qquad\mathbb E|Z_j-z_0|^4=1=B^4.                           \tag{7}
\]
Finally, \(\mathbb EB_{1i}(0)=1/2=m_1(z_0)\), so transport holds.  Equations
(3)--(7) verify every clause of the fixed-query class, giving labelled points
\(\xi^{(0)},\xi^{(1)}\).  Taking the query identically \(1/2\) yields panel
laws \(P^{(0)},P^{(1)}\) satisfying the panel class without invoking a null
conditional version.

The joint law of \(((X_{1t})_t,(Q_{1ti})_{t,i},(Z_j)_j)\) is common to the
two kernels.  Definition \texttt{def:target}, (5), and
\(\mathbb E\varepsilon_i=0\) give \(\tau(z_0)=0\) under both.  Nevertheless,
independence of \(\varepsilon_i\) from \(\mathcal X\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb K_0}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X)=0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb K_1}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X)
 =\tfrac1{16}.                                                \tag{8}
\]
This is the required explicit certificate: centering removes the obsolete
common-design shock but does not determine the remaining event-noise
constant.
